activeRoute.pointer: the operator-set active model route is persisted in the bridge SQLite store (route_state table), additively; config.json is never rewritten while a daemon is live
activeRoute.effective: the stored pointer when set, otherwise the configured defaultModelRoute; initial default is flash-max
activeRoute.operatorControl: route list / route status / route set <route> via the authenticated loopback daemon and CLI; requires the daemon running
activeRoute.noRestart: route set applies to new spawns immediately, without a daemon restart
activeRoute.offlineBehavior: route commands fail closed when the daemon is not running; the CLI never writes the route pointer outside the daemon process (no concurrent DB write)
activeRoute.noOverride: the MCP deepseek_spawn tool never exposes or forwards model_route; it always uses the active route, while legacy/direct HTTP callers still fail closed on a conflicting override
activeRoute.noFallback: no automatic fallback route ever applies

routes.modelRouteOnSpawn: not available on the MCP spawn tool; it always uses the active route. The legacy/direct HTTP contract still validates an explicitly named route with typed unknown_route, route_disabled or route_override_denied failures and never falls back
routes.pinnedPerAgent: the chosen route is persisted on the agent; continue, approval resume/reply, graceful finalization, recovery and reconciliation always use the persisted route, never mutable live defaults, and never the mutable active-route pointer
routes.legacyCompatibility: agents without a pinned route keep dispatching on their persisted flat provider/model/variant columns

errors.propagation: stable machine-readable codes flow through HTTP bodies and MCP structuredContent without text sniffing

contextFiles.prevalidation: containment, existence, regular readable file and bounded size are validated before any workspace/worktree/session/job side effect; rejected input returns a typed 400 and never creates an orphan worktree

visualContext.semantics: textual only; optional string on spawn and continue, no default. The orchestrator inspects visuals itself and sends three labeled parts ('Direct observations:', 'Interpretation:', 'Uncertainty:'). DeepSeek never receives pixels; direct observations are evidence, interpretation is a hypothesis, and details absent from the context must not be invented

antigravity.asyncContract: deepseek_spawn returns an accepted pending obligation immediately after job creation; agy runs asynchronously and deepseek_follow observes completion/failure/abort; abort between job creation and dispatch prevents the launch and never re-activates a closed/aborted agent; no provider fallback
antigravity.sandbox: antigravitySandbox (boolean, default false) enables agy --sandbox; never implied by other flags
antigravity.command: antigravityCommand (string, default null): per-bridge override for the agy executable, a bare command name (PATH lookup) or an absolute path to a trusted local executable; null keeps the default agy.exe/agy PATH lookup; a single executable, never a shell command line; whitespace-containing non-absolute values are rejected at config load, while absolute executable paths with spaces remain allowed; avoids global PATH changes
antigravity.addDirs: antigravityAddDirs (absolute string paths, default []) mounts explicit writable directories into the sandbox; relative entries are dropped at load
antigravity.autoApprove: antigravityAutoApprovePermissions (boolean, default false) passes --dangerously-skip-permissions so agy never blocks on interactive permission prompts; independent of antigravitySandbox (an unsandboxed run can carry auto-approval and a sandboxed run can omit it) and never broadens the sandbox
antigravity.recovery: antigravity runs live inside the daemon process; after a daemon loss, stranded active antigravity jobs (dispatching/running/following/finalizing) are terminalized as failed with a clear reason at startup recovery, never left dispatching/working; an orphaned child process is not controllable; in-process follow/abort semantics are unchanged
antigravity.secrets: the bridge never reads, writes or exposes Antigravity credentials or secrets

obligations.consumption: terminal results become consumed when follow/recover returns a usable final result (persisted per job); needs_approval stays pending
obligations.agentCloseSeparate: closing the agent is separate from consuming the obligation
obligations.respawn: deepseek_continue accepts allow_respawn (optional boolean, default false) as the explicit closed-agent recovery: only when the agent was closed AFTER a terminal job with a persisted result and was NOT explicitly aborted does it automatically create a NEW agent and NEW OpenCode session with persisted lineage (parent_agent_id), reusing only the parent's topic, workspace path, workspace strategy and pinned model route; thread/turn correlation hints are preserved or derived; auditable activity is recorded on both agents; the response returns the NEW agentId/jobId; the closed agent is never reopened
respawnFailClosed: flag absent on a closed agent (409 not_continuable)
doctorWarnings: genuine stale follow windows only (no false positives for fresh or auto-armed jobs; no auto-close)

retention.autoGate: auto only enables pruning on a provably empty database
retention.intrinsicGate: online pruning on a non-empty legacy database requires the in-database offline-preparation marker written by `retention dry-run` or `retention enabled --confirm`; a hand-edited retentionMode=enabled alone never arms pruning
protections: activity floor of 50 newest rows per agent
retention.metrics: dry-run and real passes report accurate protected counts (rows never eligible for pruning); doctor never claims zero protected when protected rows exist
safety: PASSIVE WAL checkpoint only, never an online VACUUM
legacy prune indexes created only by the offline CLI path
